claims.assertion: The trip was off the optimal route: actual distance 9.3 km against an optimal 3.9 km, +5.4 km (+136%), and the ride took 26.5 min against an 8 min estimate (+18.8 min).
Segment 14:10–14:13 drove 1.63 km where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, adding 1.63 km and straying up to 816 m from the optimal route; this segment is not excused by anything the rider agreed to.
Segment 14:17–14:29 drove 3.60 km where the optimal route covers 0.77 km, adding 2.83 km and straying up to 1553 m from the optimal route.

Fare fact F6 quantifies the excess distance billed at $7.58 (5.4 km × $1.41/km), and F9 shows the metered total of $25.40 included distance $13.14 for 9.3 km, so the off-route km was charged into the meter fare; under RD-2 the rider is refunded Σ extra_km × per-km rate on unexempted segments.

The driver's own reroute proposal concerned only 'go round by Cavenagh' (F10), and the rider's reply agreed to that plus a 7-Eleven stop on the way (F11); the agreement therefore cannot cover the 3.60 km / extra 2.83 km off-route run out to Beach Road at 14:17–14:29 (F5), which added up to 1553 m of detour away from the optimal route.

The rider named no location for the stop, the driver chose the 7-Eleven on Beach Road himself (F14) and did not tell the rider that this location before the deviation, so the detour km travelled to reach it is not exempted by the rider's 'stop at a 7-Eleven' request.

The driver's post-trip claim that Orchard was jammed after an accident is contradicted in part by the only accepted traffic evidence: the accident record F18 is 30 m from the optimal route and is dated 13:52, outside the trip window (pickup 14:05, drop-off 14:31), and no traffic incident fact covers the 14:17–14:29 Beach Road segment; F15/F16/F17 are only speed-band records that do not by themselves exempt a reroute.

The driver's statement that the rider 'agreed' (F14) is a claim only, not consent recorded from the rider before the segment; under RD-5 it cannot exempt any segment, and F13 confirms the chat record is complete and every message timestamped, so the consent question can be decided on the written messages F10–F12.

The amount refundable is the extra km on the unexempted segments at the meter rate: (1.63 + 2.83) km × $1.41/km = $6.29, consistent with the per-km rate evidenced by F6's $7.58 for 5.4 km and F9's $13.14 for 9.3 km.

The 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 was 2995 m from the pickup and 2098 m from the drop-off (F2), i.e. not a pickup wait; the $1.08 wait billed (F7) corresponds to that mid-trip stop, which is not a published Ryde charge for a non-RydeTAXI-style mid-trip stop and is in any event part of the off-route detour run at 14:17–14:29 (F5).

The driver has 1 upheld dispute in the last 90 days, including a no-show violation (F21); together with this established route violation, an account-review flag is warranted under RD-6 as a repeated-violation signal.

weaknesses: F10/F18: the driver did flag bad Orchard traffic before departing, and an accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed was recorded at 13:52 (F18) — the driver will argue the initial Cavenagh reroute (segment F4) was justified under RD-4(a)/(c), which could exempt the 1.63 km segment and cut our recoverable amount.

F11: the rider's own message says 'Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' — the driver will argue the rider asked for a stop and that the Beach Road stop was merely a stop, and that the rider should have named a specific 7-Eleven; the difference in outcome turns on RD-3(b) (driver chose the location without telling the rider beforehand) and RD-5 (whether 'round by Cavenagh' covers the Beach Road run).
F15: Orchard Road was recorded at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10, which supports the driver's congestion narrative even though band facts alone cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b).

F7/F9: the $1.08 waiting and the meter time component $5.81 were incurred partly at the mid-trip stop; for a metered RydeTAXI RD-3(c) says waiting units are collected and not refunded, so the wait fee may stand even if the distance portion is refunded.

claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered trip (9.3 km actual vs 3.9 km optimal, total charged $25.40), so any route-deviation refund is measured in extra kilometres at the metered per-km rate, and the per-km rate is shown by the fare itself as $1.41/km ($13.14 distance fare ÷ 9.3 km).

The first deviation, 14:10–14:13, adding 1.63 km (F4), occurred while the optimal route's Orchard Road was in speed band 1 (0–9 km/h, severe congestion) from 14:00–14:10, and an LTA-reported accident 30 m from the optimal route on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah with two lanes closed was reported at 13:52 and remained listed during the trip window.

Before leaving the optimal route the driver asked the rider about rerouting — Chat #1 at 14:01: 'Hi, traffic on Orchard is bad, ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' — and the rider answered at 14:02 'Sure' (Chat #2); both messages are timestamped and precede the first off-route segment that begins at 14:10, so the Cavenagh detour (the 1.63 km segment) was mutually agreed in advance.

The rider's own message asked only for a stop at 'a 7-Eleven on the way' without naming a location, and the driver selected the 7-Eleven on Beach Road without telling the rider the location beforehand, so the second deviation (14:17–14:29, +2.83 km, up to 1553 m off route) is NOT covered by the rider's stop request; the driver accepts that this segment's extra distance is not exempt.

The stationary 4 min 10 s at (1.3025, 103.8638) from 14:20–14:24 is the un-named 7-Eleven stop itself, 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, and it coincides with the second off-route segment rather than being a separate unexplained pause.

Because this is a RydeTAXI trip, the stop's waiting time is chargeable as metered waiting time under RD-3(c) and is not refundable; the billed waiting fee of $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) should stand, while any refund is limited to excess distance only.

The refund on the unexempt second segment is 2.83 extra km × $1.41/km = $3.99 (excess distance billed for the whole trip was $7.58 = 5.4 km × $1.41/km), with the remainder of the excess attributable to the traffic-justified Cavenagh reroute.

The driver's record (4.0 years, 4.7 rating, 812 trips/90 d, 1 upheld dispute which was no-show, route disputes upheld 0) shows no repeated route-deviation finding, so the RD-6 flag_account trigger is not met and no account flag is warranted.

There is no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in the chat or the complaint (which is a fare/routing complaint only), so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation to a human is required.

weaknesses: The driver still breached the shortest-and-most-direct obligation on the second segment: the Beach Road 7-Eleven stop was chosen by the driver, was never named to the rider before the diversion, and the rider only asked for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' (F11, F14) — the judge can find under RD-3(b)/RD-1 that 2.83 extra km is unexplained, and the rider's overcharge complaint (F5, F6) will be read alongside that.

The rider's consent (F11) is explicitly tied to going 'round by Cavenagh'; the driver drove far beyond that (up to 1553 m off the optimal route, +136% total distance, +18.8 min) (F1, F3, F5), so the judge may find the Beach Road leg falls outside the scope of the consent even on the driver's own account.

The driver's reliance on the accident (F18) covers only the first, 1.63 km segment; nothing in the traffic facts justifies the second diversion away from the route, and RD-4(b) band evidence alone is expressly not sufficient to exempt a segment (F15, F17).

Part of the excess is not clearly attributable: total excess is 5.4 km (F1) while the two segments sum to 4.46 km, and the residual is not refundable under RD-2, but a judge could attribute more of the billed excess distance (F6) to the unexempt Beach Road deviation.

The billed waiting fee (F7) sits inside an off-route segment rather than at pickup/drop-off, so the judge may question whether the stop's duration was reasonable under RD-3(c) even though RydeTAXI metered waiting is chargeable.

points.response: Agreed: the metered per-km rate is $1.41/km ($13.14 distance fare ÷ 9.3 km, F9) and RD-2 refunds the extra km of unexempted segments at that rate; our dispute is only about which segments are exempt.

Partly conceded on the 1.63 km segment (F4): the accident record F18 is 30 m from the optimal route and Orchard Road was band 1 (F15), so we no longer seek refund of that segment's extra km; however RD-4(a) requires the incident to be 'listed' in the trip window, while F18's own reported_at is 13:52, and F15/F16/F17 are band facts which under RD-4(b) are corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment on their own.

We accept the trip was longer than optimal (F1: 9.3 km vs 3.9 km, +5.4 km; F3: 26.5 min vs 8 min), but RD-1 does not make every deviation a breach — both segments must be tested against RD-4/RD-5/RD-3, and the first one is justified by the 13:52 accident report 30 m from the optimal route on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah with two lanes closed (F18) plus speed band 1 on Orchard Road 14:00–14:10 (F15).
